mechanism.plausibility_rationale: Intraoperative floppy iris syndrome (IFIS) is a well-documented clinical complication strongly associated with the use of alpha-1 adrenergic receptor antagonists, particularly tamsulosin, which targets the alpha-1A receptor subtype. The mechanism involves the blockade of alpha-1 receptors in the iris dilator muscle, leading to poor pupil dilation and iris instability during cataract surgery.
